Module 2

Install and read packages

Before we start

R on its own can do a great deal, but the work you will actually do, reading a csv, cleaning names, drawing a chart, comes from packages that other people have written. A package is like a bag of tools: you buy the bag once, and you open it every time you want what is inside. Those two moments need two different commands, and mixing them up is the most common beginner error in R. In this lecture you will learn install.packages("name"), which downloads the bag onto this computer once and for all, and library(name), which opens it at the start of every session. By the end you will know why "could not find function" almost never means the package is missing, and exactly which of the two lines you forgot.

Three boards to read, a short recap, then ten situations to try yourself.

The lecture, board by board

Three boards, in order, with a note on what to look at on each.

1A package is a bag, a library is what is inside

Start on the left: a package is the bag, and the library is the set of tools inside it. Follow the middle panel and you see the two moments that matter, getting the bag once and opening it every session, then the right hand column on why packages are worth the trouble.

2tidyverse: one box, many tools

The same idea for the one package you will use most. The box holds dplyr, ggplot2, tidyr, readr, stringr and purrr, and a single library(tidyverse) opens all of them. Read the four numbered panels in order: install once, load every session, then use any tool inside.

3Ten packages, installed and read

Ten packages you will actually meet, each with its install line and its library line side by side. Notice the pattern repeating down the board: quotes on the install, no quotes on the library, every single time.

Recap before you try

The three posters come down to two commands, used at two different moments. Read this once, then do the ten scenarios below.

  • A package is the bag. The library is what is inside it: the functions you use.
  • install.packages("name") downloads the bag onto this computer. Once, ever.
  • library(name) opens the bag. Every session, because closing R closes the bag.
  • Install takes quotes around the name. library does not.
  • "could not find function" almost always means the package is installed but not yet opened.
1Step 1
install.packages("tidyverse")
# downloading... this takes a few minutes

Once per computer. The name is text, so it needs quotes. Do this again only when a new version comes out, never at the top of a script.

2Step 2
library(tidyverse)
-- Attaching core tidyverse packages -- dplyr, ggplot2, readr, stringr, tidyr...

Every session. No quotes here. The message lists the tools that are now ready, which is the box being opened.

3Step 3
read_csv("routine_cases_dummy.csv")
Rows: 1249 Columns: 12

Now a function from inside the bag works. Before the library line, this same command would have said "could not find function".

4Step 4
search()
[1] ".GlobalEnv" "package:dplyr" "package:ggplot2" ...

If you are unsure whether a package is open, ask. search() lists everything loaded in this session, and help(name) explains any package before you use it.

Your turn: ten scenarios

Each one is a situation with a person and a folder. Write the line of R they need and press Check. The marking is exact: every bracket, quote and capital letter has to be right, just as R requires. Spacing is the only thing forgiven.

Opening the bag, not buying it again. No quotes needed here.
